newsitem.title: SPAIN: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE ON POLE FOR WILLIAMS IN SPAIN.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE ON POLE FOR WILLIAMS IN SPAIN.

text.p: Canadian Jacques Villeneuve set a new qualifying lap record and secured his fifth pole position of the season on Saturday in qualifying for Sunday's Spanish Grand Prix.
Villeneuve outpaced his Williams team-mate Heinz-Harald Frentzen to clinch his eighth pole position of his career.
The Canadian clocked a fastest time of one minute and 16.525 seconds with just three minutes of the session remaining.

His time cut more than four seconds off the previous record pole time set by Briton Damon Hill in a Williams last year -- another comprehensive demonstration of the increased speed of this year's cars as a result of the tyre war between Goodyear and Bridgestone.

Villeneuve was just two-tenths of a second faster than Frentzen, whose Spanish mother makes him the nearest thing to a local driver in the field, with Briton David Coulthard third for McLaren ahead of Frenchman Jean Alesi in a Benetton.

His pole also extended the Williams team's domination of the prime grid position to 10 successive races stretching back to last year's Hungarian Grand Prix on the 20th anniversary of the team's first race, the Spanish Grand Prix of 1977.
